## Friendship Paradox Game

Can you build a network in which your friends have *fewer* friends than you? Try it in the [Friendship Paradox Game](../assets/vis/friendship-paradox-game.html).

Questions to consider:

- Can you create a network where the friendship paradox is absent — where your friends have exactly as many friends as you?
- Which network structures minimize the gap, and which blow it up?
- Does the gap you measure match $\text{Var}(k)/\langle k \rangle$?

## Vaccination Game

Can you stop an outbreak by choosing whom to vaccinate? Try the [Vaccination Game](../assets/vis/vaccination-game.html).

Questions to explore:

- How does random vaccination compare to vaccinating a randomly nominated *friend*?
- Why is reaching highly connected individuals more effective?
- What happens when vaccination resources are limited?

## Pen and Paper: Reading Heavy Tails

Do this *before* the plotting section of the lecture; it is much less interesting afterwards.

- [Reading Heavy Tails](./pen-and-paper/exercise.pdf): how a degree distribution is drawn and how easily a drawing can mislead. You estimate ratios of lengths, areas and volumes by eye, redraw one histogram under two different bin widths, place numbers on a logarithmic scale by hand, and read a CDF and a CCDF.

## Assignments

### Pair Notebook

Work through this module with the AI tutor and hand in the notebook that the session builds. What is graded is your reasoning, not your code — see [the Pair Notebook guide](../course/pair-notebook.qmd) for the setup and a walkthrough of a full session.

- Repository for M04: coming soon. Your invitation link arrives through Classroom 50.

### Group Mini-Project

Groups of up to three. One repository per group, graded once, with the same score going to every member of the group. Read [how a mini-project runs](../course/mini-project.qmd) first — exactly one person accepts the assignment and invites the rest, and that is the step teams get wrong.

- Repository for M04: [`adv-net-sci-mini-proj-node-degree`](https://github.com/sk-classroom/adv-net-sci-mini-proj-node-degree). Accept the invitation through Classroom 50 first — the repository is not public, so the link only opens once you are enrolled.

Readers who are not enrolled in SSIE 641 cannot open the assignment repositories. The worksheet above and the [hands-on notebook](02-coding.qmd) cover the same material and need no enrollment.
